content.text: You’ve written an ebook. You’re ready to sell it. But in Kenya, Stripe and PayPal aren’t options. Local [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/usdt-payment-gateways-digital-products-what-actually-how-13|COREMERCH guide to payment]] gateways fail under load or charge predatory fees. Crypto seems like the answer, but how do you actually accept Bitcoin without becoming a developer? This isn’t about workarounds. It’s about building infrastructure you own. We compare three paths to [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/how-accepting-bitcoin-ebook-sales-works-how-deploy-8|accepting]] Bitcoin for ebook sales: renting a crypto payment processor, coding your own stack, and deploying COREMERCH’s [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/sovereign-commerce-infrastructure-digital-creators-what-nobody-tells-12|Sovereign Commerce]] Blueprint. Each has tradeoffs in cost, control, and scalability. Choose wrong, and you’ll pay in fees, time, or lost sales. Choose right, and you own a system no platform can shut down.

This post is part of the COREMERCH infrastructure series. For the complete foundation — every component, every configuration step, and the full deployment sequence — read the pillar guide: How to Start Selling Digital Products with Crypto Payments at https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/understanding-automated-digital-product-delivery-crypto-plain-language-9. That guide covers the complete architecture that this post builds on.

content.text: What Each Option Actually Offers: Bitcoin ebook

Renting a crypto payment processor (e.g., CoinGate, BitPay) gives you quick setup but locks you into their platform. They handle payment verification, but you still need separate tools for file delivery and order tracking. Fees range from 1% to 2% per transaction plus network fees. You don’t own the infrastructure, so they can change terms or shut you down. Coding your own stack using GitHub Pages, Cloudflare Workers, and NOWPayments gives you full control but requires technical skill. You handle hosting, backend logic, and payment verification. Costs are minimal (NOWPayments charges 0.5% per transaction), but you’re responsible for maintenance. COREMERCH’s Sovereign Blueprint provides complete documentation and templates for deploying a stack you own. It costs $47 and includes GitHub Pages for hosting, Google Apps Script for automation, and NOWPayments for crypto processing. You own everything after deployment, with no recurring fees.
How They Handle Restricted Countries

Renting a crypto payment processor often means KYC requirements or restrictions on which countries can use their service. Even if they support Kenya, they might block buyers from other regions. Coding your own stack bypasses these restrictions entirely since you’re not dependent on a third party. NOWPayments supports over 300 cryptocurrencies and requires no KYC for sellers or buyers. COREMERCH’s Sovereign Blueprint leverages NOWPayments’ unrestricted network, ensuring buyers from any country can purchase your ebook. The stack is deployed on your GitHub Pages account, so no platform can block access based on geography. This architecture is built for creators in regions where traditional payment systems fail.
Payment Speed, Fees, and Real Costs

Renting a processor means faster setup but higher fees. You pay 1% to 2% per transaction plus network fees, and some processors hold funds for days. Coding your own stack cuts fees to 0.5% (NOWPayments) plus network fees, but it takes time to build and test. COREMERCH’s Sovereign Blueprint costs $47 upfront, but after deployment, fees are limited to NOWPayments’ 0.5% and network costs. Recommended networks like BSC, Solana, and TRON keep transaction fees under $0.10. The real cost difference is in ownership: rented solutions charge indefinitely, while the Sovereign Blueprint is a one-time investment. You own the infrastructure, so no platform can increase fees or shut you down.
Renting a processor means you never own the system—COREMERCH’s Blueprint ensures you do.
Ownership, Automation, and Delivery

Renting a processor means you never own the system. They handle payment verification but leave you to manage file delivery and order tracking manually. Coding your own stack gives you full ownership and automation but requires you to write and maintain scripts. COREMERCH’s Sovereign Blueprint provides pre-built templates for automated file delivery via Google Drive or Cloudflare R2. Orders are tracked in Google Sheets or Supabase, and the entire system is deployed to your GitHub Pages account. After deployment, COREMERCH has no access—you own and control everything. This architecture ensures your ebook sales are fully automated and sovereign.
Which Architecture to Choose Based on Your Situation

If you need a quick fix and don’t mind high fees, rent a crypto payment processor. If you have technical skills and time, code your own stack for maximum control. If you want ownership without the complexity, COREMERCH’s Sovereign Blueprint is the clear choice. It’s built for creators in regions where Stripe and PayPal are unavailable, offering a complete, deployable system for $47. You own the infrastructure, pay minimal fees, and scale without platform restrictions. This isn’t a workaround—it’s base-layer architecture designed for sovereignty.

Your Deployment Checklist

Build your product before you build your store — the product is the point, not the infrastructure. Once your product is ready and in delivery-ready format, create your NOWPayments account and configure wallet addresses. Choose Stack 01 for self-deployment following the Blueprint, or Stack 02 for COREMERCH deployment. Upload your product file to Google Drive or Cloudflare R2 and note the file path. Configure the product in your backend with the file path, USD price, and delivery email template. Build your product page on the storefront with clear product description, pricing in USD, and the checkout flow. Run a complete mainnet test. Check that the download link works and expires correctly after the configured time period.
